Augustus.text: Augustus McCrae, Call's talkative, Latin-boasting partner in the Hat Creek outfit and a former Ranger, left the drive alone to track Blue Duck after Lorena was taken. On the Canadian he survived an ambush, then with July Johnson stormed the outlaw camp, killed the gang and freed Lorena, though Blue Duck escaped. He is now riding east with the weakened Lorena to wait for the herd.

Pea Eye.text: Pea Eye is a loyal, plainspoken hand who rangered under Call and Augustus and still carries old wounds and dreams from Indian fights. He works the Hat Creek drive under Call, helped regather the herd after its stampedes, and with Gus still missing is camped with the crew in Indian Territory, just north of the Red River crossing.

Call.text: Captain Call, the stern former Ranger who co-owns the Hat Creek outfit with Augustus, is leading a herd gathered from Mexico north from Lonesome Dove toward Montana. Brooding and solitary, he hired the cook Po Campo and pushed the herd past Fort Worth while Gus chased Blue Duck. He now camps apart from the crew just north of the Red River, fearing his partner has vanished on the plains.

Newt.text: Newt is the youngest hand in the Hat Creek outfit, a Lonesome Dove boy whose late mother was Maggie, eager to prove himself a man to the Captain. He still grieves his friend Sean, lost his horse Mouse while secretly watching over Lorena, and has weathered stampedes and drenching storms. He is camped with the herd just north of the Red River.

Lorena.text: Lorena, a young prostitute from the Dry Bean who dreams of cool San Francisco, left Lonesome Dove with Jake Spoon, who turned cruel and left her alone near Austin. Blue Duck kidnapped her, and she suffered terribly in his Canadian River camp until Augustus rescued her. Weak and shaken, she is riding east with Gus along the Canadian to wait for Call's herd.

Lippy.text: Lippy is the Dry Bean's piano player, a St. Louis native in a battered bowler, who signed on to the Hat Creek drive and was put in charge of the horses. He survived the wagon flipping onto him near San Antonio and, frightened of snakes since Sean's death, keeps to the wagon. He was last noted with the outfit moving north after Augustus rode off.

Dish Boggett.text: Dish Boggett is a proud, skilled cowboy from Matagorda who has trailed herds north before and joined the Hat Creek outfit while hopelessly in love with Lorena, who chose Jake. He has ridden through the drive's storms and stampedes, scoffing at rivers and calling the Red the next excitement. He is camped with the crew just north of it in Indian Territory.

Deets.text: Deets is the Hat Creek outfit's trusted scout and tracker, a veteran of the Ranger days who was sad to leave Lonesome Dove's quiet life. Named scout by Call, he finds water and safe crossings, tried to trail Blue Duck, and most recently found a gravel bar that let the herd cross the feared Red River. He is camped with the crew just north of it.

Jake Spoon.text: Jake Spoon, a charming gambler and old Ranger comrade of Call and Augustus, fled Arkansas after accidentally killing Fort Smith's mayor and sparked the Montana drive. He took Lorena north beside the herd but mistreated her, lingered gambling in Austin, and returned to find her gone. He is now gambling in Fort Worth, snubbing the Hat Creek hands.

July Johnson.text: July Johnson, the young sheriff of Fort Smith, set out after Jake Spoon for his brother Ben's death but turned to searching for his runaway wife Elmira. On the Canadian he helped Augustus rescue Lorena, then found Roscoe, Joe and Janey murdered at his camp. Grieving, he has crossed the Canadian and ridden north alone to keep hunting for Elmira.

Wilbarger.text: Wilbarger is a hard-bitten trail boss who recovered his stolen horses from the Hat Creek outfit at Lonesome Dove, boasting of Yale Latin, before driving three thousand head north. Meeting July near Fort Worth, he said Jake was coming north and offered Joe work. He was last seen riding alone ahead of his herd to check the Red River.

Allen O'Brien.text: Allen O'Brien is one of two Irish brothers Call found lost and hungry in Mexico and took on as hands; he pines for his young wife Sary back in Ireland. His brother Sean died among water moccasins at the Nueces. Allen has stayed with the drive through Fort Worth and the Red River crossing and is camped with the crew in Indian Territory.

Jasper Fant.text: Jasper Fant is a gloomy cowboy from up the Rio Grande who joined the Hat Creek drive and constantly dreads drowning in the rivers ahead. He has made it through the Nueces and later crossings, went carousing in Fort Worth and paid with a fierce hangover, and is now camped with the outfit in Indian Territory just north of the Red River.

Needle Nelson.text: Needle Nelson, a hand from north of San Antonio, joined the Hat Creek outfit and fretted early that a late start would mean crossing the Yellowstone on ice. He has stood night guard, ridden out stampedes, and caroused in Fort Worth, where he mocked a hungover Jasper. He is now camped with the herd just north of the Red River.

Bert Borum.text: Bert Borum is a cheerful hand from Brownsville who signed on with the Hat Creek outfit back in Lonesome Dove. He has ridden through the drive's stampedes, storms and river crossings, joined the carousing at Fort Worth, and helped push the herd over the Red River. He is camped with the crew in Indian Territory.

Soupy Jones.text: Soupy Jones is a cowboy who rode into the Hat Creek camp just as the drive was starting, fresh from Bastrop where his wife had died, and was hired on the spot. He has stayed with the herd through stampedes, Fort Worth and the Red River crossing, and is now camped with the outfit just north of the Red in Indian Territory.

Peach.text: Peach is the widow of Ben, Fort Smith's mayor and July Johnson's brother, whom Jake Spoon accidentally shot. She pushed July to chase the killer, found Elmira's cabin empty and sent Roscoe after July, and wrote July with the news. She remains in Fort Smith.

Joe.text: Joe is a Fort Smith boy whom Elmira insisted July take along on his pursuit of Jake Spoon. He rode with July into Texas, was offered work by Wilbarger, and joined Roscoe and Janey going north to look for Elmira. Left waiting at a camp on the Canadian, he was killed there by a night intruder and buried on the plain above.

Elmira.text: Elmira is July Johnson's wife, a woman with a hard past in the Kansas cow towns, who while secretly pregnant slipped out of Fort Smith on a whiskey traders' boat to escape her marriage. After a violent trip up the Arkansas, she left Bent's Fort with Big Zwey and is driving a patched hide wagon across the plains toward Ogallala.

Roscoe Brown.text: Roscoe Brown was July Johnson's reluctant deputy in Fort Smith, pushed by the town to ride after July with word that Elmira had left. After a long misadventure in Texas, where the runaway Janey joined him and outlaws robbed him, he found July and went north with him. He was killed by a night intruder at July's Canadian River camp and buried there.

Fowler.text: Fowler is one of the whiskey traders whose boat carried Elmira up the Arkansas River from Fort Smith onto the plains. At Bent's Fort he told her of Ogallala on the Platte, and he plans to head back downriver the following week.

Janey.text: Janey was a runaway girl, traded to a cruel old man in north Texas, who escaped and joined Roscoe, treating his stings and catching food. Resourceful and stubborn, she pelted the outlaws robbing him with rocks and followed July's party on foot. She was killed with Roscoe and Joe by a night intruder at the camp on the Canadian.

Blue Duck.text: Blue Duck is a feared outlaw who once led Comanchero raids along the Red River and menaced Augustus at Lorena's camp. He kidnapped Lorena, gave her over to abuse in his Canadian River camp, and sent men to ambush Gus, who then wiped out the gang. Blue Duck slipped away toward the river and is at large, perhaps heading for Colorado.

Po Campo.text: Po Campo is the odd Mexican cook Call hired, who walked into camp with his donkey and quickly won the crew over with plover-egg omelets and fried grasshoppers. He once raised sheep on the Llano Estacado until Blue Duck killed his three sons. He is now cooking for the outfit camped just north of the Red River.
